# Incident Response
Incidents are graded by how much harm they could do to the Company, not by how dangerous they are to the officer. The higher the category, the less the Company can afford to have anyone talk about it, and the further Security is expected to go to make sure nobody does.
The Sergeant decides the category and may raise it at any time. Categories 4 and 5 require the senior employee's authority. If the senior employee can't be reached, the Sergeant acts and reports afterwards.
## Category 1: Minor [italic]Trespass, disorderly visitors, petty theft, damage to Company property.[/italic] - Remove the person from Company areas and recover anything taken. - Record their name and what happened. - Repeat offenders may be detained and questioned.
## Category 2: Moderate [italic]Theft of valuable property, assault on staff, armed intruders, break-ins.[/italic] - Detain the offender and recover the property. - Treat any injured staff and report casualties to the Sergeant. - Hand the offender to colonial law enforcement once the senior employee agrees. The Company decides what charges it wants to press.
## Category 3: Serious [italic]Theft of Company data or research, leaks to colonists or the press, sabotage, staff killed on Company property.[/italic] - Seal the area. Nobody enters or leaves without the Sergeant's approval. - Detain everyone involved and every witness who isn't Company staff. - Recover every copy of the stolen material: papers, disks, recordings and photographs. Search everyone who was present. - Witnesses are kept on site until the senior employee has spoken to them. Most can be persuaded to remember things differently. - Staff deaths are recorded as workplace accidents until the senior employee decides otherwise.
## Category 4: Severe [italic]Containment failure, a colonist who has seen restricted research or a specimen, evidence of Company research reaching colonial authorities.[/italic] - Lock down the site. All Company areas are closed, and outside communications from Company areas are stopped. - Contain the hazard first and the people second. Specimens are to be recaptured or killed. Recapture is preferred, but not at any cost. - Every outsider who knows what happened is detained and held until the senior employee decides what to do with them. They are not to be released while the matter is open. - Recordings, notes and samples taken by anyone outside the Company are confiscated or destroyed. - The senior employee may request contractors through PMC Dispatch. Security secures the landing zone for them. - Colonists are told only the approved explanation (see [textlink="Site Recovery" link="CMUHandbookSecurityRecovery"/]).
## Category 5: Critical [italic]An uncontained outbreak, or any situation in which the Company's involvement can no longer be kept from the colony or the outside world.[/italic]
At Category 5 the site is already lost. Security's task is to make sure that nothing that could be traced back to the Company leaves it. - Research staff, their data and the senior employee are evacuated first, in that order, on the first available Company transport. - Anything that can't be taken is destroyed: samples, specimens, research records, terminals and their data. - Nobody outside the Company who knows what happened leaves the site. The senior employee gives the order, and Security carries it out. - Security personnel leave last, once the senior employee confirms nothing remains to be done. - What happened at the site is never discussed again, with anyone.
